source.citation: Resendiz-Infante & Gauthier 2024, Frontiers in Bird Science
methods_basis: St. Lawrence Valley treated as one spring stopover
Nunavik and Baffin Island are the two intermediate Arctic stopover regions
three stopover polygons were refined from tracking/survey/literature with vegetation and elevation layers
Bylot south plain is the breeding target rather than a staging risk context

source_seasonal_windows.St_Lawrence: 1 Apr-15 May; 1-15 May is the source-defined shorter sensitivity window

mapping_rule.spatial_assignment: assign each habitat by its geometric centroid to exactly one source-region polygon
mapping_rule.accepted_polygon_source: the three stopover polygons used by Resendiz-Infante & Gauthier 2024, or an exact author/source release of those geometries
mapping_rule.outside_all_polygons: exclude from primary risk set and count in audit
mapping_rule.intersects_multiple_polygons: fail closed; do not choose nearest polygon

geometry_gate.consequence: do not execute focal GPS cue-uptake outcome until source-backed region geometry is available
public_source_findings: article Methods describe polygon construction/refinement but provide no GIS vertices
Supplementary Material documents migration timing and related analyses but no exact stopover polygon object was located
publisher Figure 1 is a raster visualization and remains sensitivity-only under the frozen protocol
article Data Availability directs further inquiries to the corresponding author
geometry_gate.next_primary_route: exact author/source release or other exact source-backed geometry only

rationale: q is defined at shared route-region scale, so behavioral context must be the same shared ecological coordinate rather than individual-specific DBSCAN habitat identity.
